Running gear (2020-2023): rigid (solid) steer-drive axles front and rear, each with an integrated electric traction motor, located by three reaction rods (3-link) plus a Panhard rod, coil springs and controlled-damping shock absorbers, 25 cm suspension stroke. Sources: Janes reposts (defencehub.live), PIAP INTARG poster, defence24.com field-test article.

Sensor layout (2020 prototype, Janes): GPS receiver, two lidars, four hull-mounted HD navigation cameras (likely one per side/corner), four drive-assistant cameras, and a PTZ camera; cameras are 'distributed around the vehicle and its robotic arm'. Source: https://defencehub.live/threads/polish-lukasiewicz-piap-unveils-hunter-ugv.1331/ and https://www.milmag.eu/news/view?news_id=4611

2020/2021 cargo-mule configuration: payload deck carrying cargo crates and an optional hydraulic arm; shown at Defence24 Day 2020 and Defence24 TV 2021 'in a cargo mule configuration'. Source: https://defence24.com/armed-forces/land/hunter-35-tonnes-hybrid-land-robot-defence24-tv

2023-2024 armed configuration: AREX ZMU-03 remote weapon station (12.7 mm M2HB plus smoke grenade launchers, day/thermal head, laser rangefinder) mounted on the top deck; turret operable from an onboard station or remotely from a portable console. Sources: overtdefense.com 2023, milmag.pl ZMU-03 articles, defence24.pl.

MSPO 2024 version: adds lidars and stereovision cameras to the ZMU-03 armed vehicle (official PIAP release https://piap.lukasiewicz.gov.pl/en/2024/09/02/lukasiewicz-piap-mobile-robots-in-new-guises-at-the-mspo/).

MSPO 2025 anti-drone version: RCWS with ZM Tarnów WLKM 12.7 mm Gatling-type gun, 400 rounds onboard, radar-cued (nano-drones detected up to 3.5 km). Source: https://milmag.pl/en/mspo-2025-piap-hunter-with-a-12-7-mm-weapon-module/

estimates.value: 2.70 m primary (2.20 m alternative to keep as a xacro arg)
estimates.reasoning: Two figures are published. 2.70 m comes from the PIAP-authored INTARG 2021 poster (via search summary), Army Recognition and Militär Aktuell. 2.20 m comes from Polish press (milmag 2020, defence24 2023 and the outlets that copied them). In several of those Polish sources width and wheelbase are both 220 cm, so the wheelbase looks like a transcription error copied from the width. Check against the overall length: 4.70 m length with 1.0 m wheels gives 1.00 m front/rear overhang from axle to bumper at 2.70 m wheelbase (0.50 m beyond the tyre), or 1.25 m at 2.20 m. Photos can settle it: at 2.7 m the gap between front and rear tyres is about 1.7 wheel diameters; at 2.2 m it is about 1.2.

Not published. Overall width is 2.20 m. A 1.0 m off-road tyre (e.g. 37x12.5R17, 335/80R20, 365/80R20 class) is about 0.31-0.37 m wide. If the tyres' outer sidewalls define the 2.20 m width, track = 2.20 - ~0.34 = ~1.86 m.

estimates.value: OD 1.00 m (r = 0.50 m unloaded, ~0.47 m static loaded), tyre width ~0.34 m, rim ~20 in
estimates.reasoning: Only the 1 m diameter is published. Width and rim are typical for 1 m military/off-road tyres carrying ~1-1.25 t per wheel.

estimates.value: hull ~1.45-1.6 m without turret; ~2.1-2.3 m with ZMU-03; no mast data
estimates.reasoning: Not published. Axle centre is at ~0.47-0.5 m. Wheel tops are at ~1.0 m, plus ~0.10-0.125 m bump travel and fender clearance, so the deck is at ~1.15-1.25 m. The hull houses the generator, 40 kWh battery and electronics, which suggests a top at ~1.45-1.6 m. ZMU-03 class turret height is ~0.6-0.7 m (estimate).

estimates.value: ~0.30 m under axle/differential housings; ~0.45-0.50 m under hull belly
estimates.reasoning: Not published. Rigid axles put the minimum clearance under the differential/motor housing: static loaded radius ~0.47 m minus a housing radius of ~0.17 m gives ~0.30 m. The belly sits higher because the axles move up into the wheel wells.

estimates.value: Base 3500 kg (2020 mule) or 4000 kg (2023+ armed). Unsprung ~2 x 300-350 kg per axle (beam + integrated motor + diff + hubs/brakes) + 4 x ~80 kg wheel/tyre, so ~950-1000 kg unsprung. Sprung chassis ~2500 kg (3.5 t) or ~3000 kg (4 t). Turret: ZMU-03 205 kg (published) or WLKM RCWS ~500 kg + ammo
estimates.reasoning: Published totals are split using typical heavy solid-axle component masses. Only the totals and the 205 kg ZMU-03 mass are published.

estimates.parameter: chassis inertia (sprung body as box 4.7 x 2.2 x 1.0 m, 3000 kg)
estimates.value: Ixx ~1460, Iyy ~5770, Izz ~6730 kg*m^2 (scale x0.83 for 2500 kg); CoM ~0.9-1.0 m above ground, roughly mid-wheelbase
estimates.reasoning: Solid-box formula I = m/12 (a^2 + b^2). Real mass is concentrated (battery, generator low and central), so 0.8-0.9 of the box values is also defensible. Generator and battery placement are not published.

estimates.value: ~12 kg*m^2 per wheel+tyre (80 kg, r_o 0.5 m, r_i ~0.25 m)
estimates.reasoning: Thick-ring approximation I = m (r_o^2 + r_i^2)/2.

estimates.value: total 0.25 m (published); suggested +0.10 m bump / -0.15 m rebound, or symmetric +/-0.125 m
estimates.reasoning: Only the total stroke is published.

Sprung mass per corner ~800-825 kg (4 t vehicle). A 1.4 Hz ride frequency (typical for off-road military wheeled vehicles) gives k = m (2*pi*f)^2 ~ 62-64 kN/m. Static sag is then g/(2*pi*f)^2 ~ 0.127 m, about half of the published 0.25 m stroke, which is self-consistent.

estimates.value: ~4.5-5.5 kN*s/m (damping ratio 0.3-0.4)
estimates.reasoning: c = 2*zeta*sqrt(k*m) with k ~62 kN/m and m ~800 kg. The real dampers are described as controlled/adjustable (semi-active).

estimates.value: Per axle: 2 lower trailing links ~0.9-1.0 m long, 1 upper central/offset link ~0.6-0.8 m, Panhard rod ~1.5-1.7 m running nearly full width
estimates.reasoning: Typical heavy solid-axle 3-link proportions. The sources confirm only the link count ('three reaction rods') and the Panhard rod. For a URDF, model each axle as a beam with prismatic (heave) + revolute (roll about the longitudinal axis) joints relative to the chassis, or as a closed-chain approximation.

estimates.value: ~30 deg (range 28-35 deg)
estimates.reasoning: Not published. This is typical for steered rigid axles with ~1 m tyres and CV joints, limited by tyre-to-body clearance within a 2.2 m width.

estimates.value: 4WS counter-phase at 30 deg, WB 2.7 m: centreline radius ~2.3 m, outer wheel path ~3.6-3.7 m radius, body swept circle ~8.3 m diameter. Front-steer only: centreline ~4.7 m. With WB 2.2 m: centreline ~1.9 m (4WS)
estimates.reasoning: Kinematics: R_centre = (WB/2)/tan(delta) for symmetric 4WS, or WB/tan(delta) for 2WS. Outer path = sqrt((R + T/2)^2 + (WB/2)^2) with T ~1.85 m. Body corner at (2.35, R + 1.1) gives the swept radius. Nothing is published.

estimates.value: ~27.8 rad/s unloaded radius (265 rpm); ~29.6 rad/s at 0.47 m loaded radius
estimates.reasoning: v = 13.9 m/s divided by the wheel radius. Use this for the URDF velocity limit (about 32 rad/s to allow 'over 50 km/h').

open_questions: WHEELBASE CONFLICT: 2.70 m (PIAP INTARG poster via search summary, Army Recognition, Militär Aktuell) vs 2.20 m (milmag 2020 PL, defence24 2023, spidersweb, wnp, tek.info). The 2.20 m figure equals the published width and may be a copied error. Confirm from side-view photos by measuring the gap between the tyres in wheel diameters (1.7 means 2.7 m, 1.2 means 2.2 m), or by reading the INTARG poster PDF if any channel can download it.
Overall height (hull, with ZMU-03, with WLKM RCWS, with mast) is not published anywhere found.
Track width, ground clearance, tyre size/brand and rim size are not published.
Max steering angle, steering modes (counter-phase, crab, front-only) and turning radius/circle are not published. Sources confirm only 'two steering axles'.
Gradient, side slope, fording depth, vertical step, trench crossing, and approach/departure angles are not published.
Fuel type and tank capacity are not published. Range 450 km on a full tank (2026 press) and 'up to 8 h' operation (Portal Obronny 2024, single source).

Mass conflict: 3.5 t (2020 prototype, mule) vs 'over 4 t' (2023+ armed). Unknown whether 4 t includes the turret, or whether the hull itself grew. Gross mass is never stated; ~4.5-5 t is implied by the ~1 t payload.

Suspension: dependent 3-link + Panhard (2020-2023, PIAP poster) vs 'independent suspension' (defence24 April 2026) vs 'active suspension' (2017-2020 project page). Unclear whether a 2025/2026 redesign happened or whether this is press error.
Drive layout: 'two steering axles - each integrated with an electric motor' plus differential locks (2 axle motors), vs one exhibitor listing that says 'independently driven wheels'.
Camera count differs by year: 9 (2020), 6 or 7 (2023/24), plus extra lidars and stereo cameras (2024). Exact mounting positions are unknown without photos.
Generator engine type (diesel per Radio Kielce 'wspomagany dieslem'), battery and generator placement, and CoM height are not published.

The INTARG 2021 poster PDF (https://www.intarg.haller.pl/targi/pliki_wynalazki/posters/157-1623325091.pdf) is the most authoritative PIAP-authored spec sheet found, but it could not be downloaded here (proxy 403). It may contain further figures (clearance, height, gradient).

visual_descriptions: 4x4 wheeled, cab-less, angular hull ~4.7 m long x 2.2 m wide on four large (~1 m) off-road tyres; two rigid (beam) axles, both steerable (Janes 2020; Defence24 2023).

Railing around the top deck carries top-view cameras; front and rear driving cameras; two side cameras on each side; a PTZ camera for panoramic view (INTARG 2021 poster / Army Recognition 2024: https://www.armyrecognition.com/archives/archives-land-defense/land-defense-2024/poland-deploys-piap-hunter-next-gen-unmanned-ground-vehicle).

2020 prototype: GPS receiver, two lidars, four hull-mounted HD navigation cameras, plus additional HD cameras incl. PTZ; shown with optional hydraulic manipulator arm, cargo crate, GPR, or UAV landing pad (Janes https://www.janes.com/defence-news/news-detail/lukasiewicz-piap-unveils-hunter-ugv ; Milmag EN https://milmag.pl/en/lukasiewicz-piap-institute-presents-hunter-ugv/).

estimates.reasoning: Three independent sources (INTARG 2021 PIAP poster, Army Recognition 2024, militaeraktuell) give 270 cm; the 220 cm figure appears only in Milmag 2020 and articles copying it, always next to 220 cm width (likely a copy error). Geometric check: with 4.7 m length and 1.0 m wheels, a 2.2 m wheelbase would leave 2.5 m of total overhang (1.25 m each end), implausible for an off-road UGV; 2.7 m leaves ~1.0 m each end (~0.5 m beyond tyre).

Tender specifies Ultimate Dana 60 with 70 in (1778 mm) WMS-to-WMS. Track = WMS - 2*wheel offset; with near-zero to slightly negative offset wheels the track is 1.78-1.85 m. Check: 1.80 m track + ~0.34 m tyre section = ~2.14 m outer tyre width, consistent with 2.2 m overall width.

estimates.reasoning: Wheel diameter 1 m (~39.4 in) and 8x6.5 in bolt pattern (light-truck/Dana 60 standard). 40x13.50R17 is the common 8-lug off-road size at ~1 m OD. Military 335/80R20 (OD ~1.05 m) is also near 1 m but typically 10-stud. Size not published; treat as assumption.

estimates.value: 17 in (0.432 m) assumed

estimates.value: ~17:1 (≈3.1:1 reduction gearbox x 5.38 axle)
estimates.reasoning: At 50 km/h a 1.0 m wheel turns 265 rpm; x5.38 = 1427 rpm at pinion. The PMSM tender requires >=4500 rpm at full load, implying an intermediate reduction of ~3.1:1 so the motor reaches ~4500 rpm at top speed. Not published.

estimates.value: ~45 kW continuous / ~110 kW peak per motor
estimates.reasoning: Total drive 90 kW cont / 220 kW peak split across 2 motors (one per axle).

estimates.value: ~4,000 Nm per wheel (traction-limited); ~1,450 Nm at each axle pinion peak
estimates.reasoning: 4,000 kg x 9.81 x mu 0.8 = 31.4 kN total tractive force x 0.5 m radius = 15.7 kNm total = ~3.9 kNm per wheel. Per axle 7.85 kNm /5.38 = 1,459 Nm at pinion; /3.1 reduction = ~470 Nm motor torque, consistent with a 110 kW PMSM peaking ~2,200 rpm.
Dana 60 front ball-joint knuckles with full-width housing typically give 35-40 deg lock (stock Ford Super Duty ~35 deg; aftermarket up to ~40 deg with 40 in tyres). Not published for HUNTeR.

estimates.value: Front-only steer: ~5.5 m outer-wheel radius; 4WS counter-phase: ~3.1-3.4 m outer-wheel radius
estimates.reasoning: L=2.7 m, track 1.8 m, delta=35 deg. Front-only: R_rear-axle-centre = L/tan(delta)=3.86 m; outer front wheel = sqrt((3.86+0.9)^2+2.7^2)=5.47 m. 4WS: R_centre=(L/2)/tan(delta)=1.93 m; outer wheel = sqrt((1.93+0.9)^2+1.35^2)=3.13 m. Wheelbase conflict: 270 cm (PIAP poster 2021, Army Recognition, militaeraktuell) vs 220 cm (Milmag 2020, Defence24 2023, wnp.pl, spidersweb). 270 cm is better supported and geometrically plausible.

visual_descriptions: Cab-less 4x4 hull about 4.7 m long and 2.2 m wide. Both axles steer, each is a rigid beam axle (Ultimate Dana 60-class front-steer axles per 2017 tender) with an integrated electric traction motor, located by a 3-link + Panhard bar with coil springs and controlled dampers giving 25 cm of travel (Janes 2020; ArmyRecognition 2024; PIAP BIP tender ZO/11/07/2017).

Sensor fit on the 2020 prototype: GPS receiver, two lidars, 9 HD cameras: one pan-tilt-zoom camera (mast/turret), 4 hull-mounted navigation cameras and 4 drive-assistant cameras (Milmag EN 2020, Janes 2020). The 2024 version adds lidars and stereovision cameras (PIAP MSPO 2024 page).

Payload options seen: cargo crates, hydraulic arm, ground-penetrating radar, UAV landing pad (Janes/Milmag 2020). Armed versions carry an AREX/WB ZMU-03 remote weapon station on the top deck (2023-2024), a ZMT WLKM 12.7 mm multi-barrel MG module (MSPO 2025), and a Belma Bluszcz scatterable-mine launcher (one or two units) on the deck (Eurosatory/MSPO 2026). There is also a counter-drone version (rp.pl 2026).
Teleoperation console uses a steering wheel and pedals (Janes 2020).

Hybrid drive allows silent, electric-only movement. A 2026 manufacturer listing cites reduced acoustic and thermal signatures in electric mode. No source found says where the genset, battery, fuel tank or exhaust sit in the hull.

estimates.value: Engine about 110-125 kW mechanical (about 150-170 hp), likely a 2.0-3.0 L automotive turbodiesel. Engine plus PM generator plus cooling plus exhaust approx. 300-400 kg (best guess 350 kg)

Diesel is the likely fuel because of NATO single-fuel policy (F-34/diesel), but no source confirms it; sources only say 'combustion' / 'generator spalinowy'.
